nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Drives plant growth on open dunes, in wetlands and in the oak woods.

nodes.name: Lake Michigan & wetlands
nodes.desc: The park runs along the lake shore, and Wikipedia says extensive wetlands fill many depressions between the dune ridges.

nodes.name: Sand dunes & soil
nodes.desc: Dunes rise to nearly 200 feet inland from the beach, and the NPS says all stages of plant succession can be seen on the youngest ones.

nodes.name: Fire
nodes.desc: Wikipedia says fire, lit by people or lightning, kept oak savannas from turning into closed forest by favouring fire-tolerant oaks.

nodes.name: Fungi & bacteria
nodes.desc: Break down dead grass, leaves, wood and carcasses and return nutrients to the sand and soil.

nodes.name: American beachgrass
nodes.desc: A beach grass native to Great Lakes shores. Wikipedia says its genus builds coastal dunes and stabilises the sand with creeping rhizomes.

nodes.name: Jack pine
nodes.desc: A pine of sandy ground, recorded often near the park and listed in GloBI as food for deer, red squirrels and white-footed mice.

nodes.name: Oaks
nodes.desc: Black oak dominates savanna on sandy soils per Wikipedia, which lists Indiana Dunes as a remnant oak savanna. Acorns feed many animals.

nodes.name: Common Milkweed
nodes.desc: A prairie wildflower and the food plant of monarch caterpillars. GloBI also records rabbits eating it.

nodes.name: Cattails
nodes.desc: Marsh plants that fill the wet hollows between dune ridges and feed muskrats.

nodes.name: White-tailed deer
nodes.desc: One of the common large animals of the park. Browses woody plants and wildflowers and supplies food for coyotes, bobcats and vultures.

nodes.name: Eastern cottontail
nodes.desc: Eats grasses and wildflowers such as milkweed, and is prey for foxes, coyotes, raccoons and bobcats.

nodes.name: American red squirrel
nodes.desc: The most-recorded mammal in the GBIF data. Eats seeds of pines and other trees and is eaten by coyotes and foxes.

nodes.name: White-footed mouse
nodes.desc: A small seed-eating rodent of woods and dune scrub that feeds snakes, foxes and coyotes.

nodes.name: Muskrat
nodes.desc: A marsh rodent that feeds on cattails and other water plants and is taken by herons, foxes, raccoons and coyotes.

nodes.name: Monarch butterfly
nodes.desc: Caterpillars feed only on milkweed, and adults sip nectar from flowers such as milkweed, buttonbush and beebalm.

nodes.name: Common garter snake
nodes.desc: A widespread snake of wet ground that eats small mammals and amphibians and is prey for herons and foxes.

nodes.name: Great blue heron
nodes.desc: Wading bird of marshes and shores. GloBI records it eating frogs, snakes, voles and muskrats.

nodes.name: Raccoon
nodes.desc: A common omnivore that GloBI records eating rabbits, muskrats, birds, frogs and snakes.

nodes.name: Red fox
nodes.desc: A common canid of the park that GloBI records preying on rabbits, squirrels, mice, muskrats and snakes.

nodes.name: Turkey vulture
nodes.desc: A scavenger that cleans up dead deer, rabbits and muskrats, as GloBI records.

nodes.name: Coyote
nodes.desc: Top mammal predator here. GloBI records it eating rabbits, squirrels, mice, muskrats, beavers and deer.

nodes.name: Bobcat
nodes.desc: Wikipedia says bobcats were photographed in the park again around 2018. A cat that hunts rabbits, rodents and young deer.
